parsed_output.answer: MATH2014A is Mathematics II (33 NQF credits, approximately 330 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA04 Year 2 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Dr Jabulani Phakathi; Prof M. Folly-Gbetoula; Prof Darlison Nyirenda. Course coordinator: Dr Jabulani Phakathi. Content covered: Algebra covering complex numbers series linear spaces orthonormality and complex variables; calculus covering differential equations vector functions scalar and vector fields path and double integrals; Laplace Fourier and special-function transform methods. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

course_information.additional_materials: Recommended texts by G. James or K. Stroud; alternatives by Zill and Cullen Jordan and Smith O'Neill Kreyszig Weir Hass and Giordano; second-year study guides tutorial questions Ulwazi and the retained first-year textbook.

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3016A is Control I (18 NQF credits, approximately 180 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA03 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Prof M. A. van Wyk; Dr M. Ngwako. Course coordinator: Prof M. A. van Wyk. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3015A is Data and Information Management (18 NQF credits, approximately 180 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA04 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Prof Ling Cheng. Course coordinator: Prof Ling Cheng. Content covered: Information laws conversion and representation; cryptography; data compression; error detection and correction; storage transmission and information security. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3009A is Software Development II (18 NQF credits, approximately 180 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA03 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Dr S. P. Levitt. Course coordinator: Dr S. P. Levitt. Content covered: Modern C++ and its development environment; object-oriented analysis design and programming; standard-library containers iterators and algorithms; programming principles; unit testing; Git and GitHub; UML and documentation; error handling and graphical user interfaces. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

reasons: CLASH_MATH2014A_ELEN3009A: ELEN3009A has a lecture timetable clash with MATH2014A, which the student is repeating, so it cannot be taken (EIE_PLANNER_2026, sheet 'EE YOS 2'; EIE_REG_GRID_2026).

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3009A is Software Development II (18 NQF credits, approximately 180 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA04 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Dr S. P. Levitt. Course coordinator: Dr S. P. Levitt. Content covered: Modern C++ and its development environment; object-oriented analysis design and programming; standard-library containers iterators and algorithms; programming principles; unit testing; Git and GitHub; UML and documentation; error handling and graphical user interfaces. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

reasons: Prerequisite rule PRE_ELEN3009 is not satisfied.

reasons: Prerequisite rule PRE_ELEN3009 is not satisfied.

course_information.additional_materials: Lospinoso C++ Crash Course; Meyers Effective Modern C++; Sutter and Alexandrescu C++ Coding Standards; Stroustrup The C++ Programming Language; C++ Core Guidelines; course website and Ulwazi.
course_information.evidence_notes: Credits and total notional hours are curriculum-derived. The CBO describes the Software Development sequence but delegates formal coded registration rules to current Faculty Rules.

hours.basis: 1 NQF credit represents 10 notional learning hours; explicit weekly guidance is quoted separately from the available course evidence.
hours.contact_pattern: Hybrid delivery using online videos and supplementary material with interactive in-person lectures laboratories a multi-week pair project and consultation.
hours.weekly_workload_guidance: No explicit weekly workload total is stated in the CBO.

course_information.prescribed_materials: No prescribed textbook stated.
course_information.scope: Modern C++ and its development environment; object-oriented analysis design and programming; standard-library containers iterators and algorithms; programming principles; unit testing; Git and GitHub; UML and documentation; error handling and graphical user interfaces.

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3013A is Signals and Systems IIB (9 NQF credits, approximately 90 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA04 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Prof O. parsed_output.answer: ELEN3016A is Control I (18 NQF credits, approximately 180 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA04 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Prof M. A. van Wyk; Dr M. Ngwako. Course coordinator: Prof M. A. van Wyk. Source: verified 2026 CBO.

parsed_output.answer: ELEN3012A is Signals and Systems IIA (12 NQF credits, approximately 120 total notional learning hours). It is taken as EFA03 Year 3 compulsory. Academic staff/lecturer(s): Dr Nyandoro O. T.; Prof Richard Ndjiongue. Course coordinator: Dr Nyandoro O. T.. hours.basis: 1 NQF credit represents 10 notional learning hours; explicit weekly guidance is quoted separately from the available course evidence.
hours.contact_pattern: Lectures with discussion worked examples current affairs and engineering business cases; no formal tutorials or laboratories; one individual and one group project.
hours.weekly_workload_guidance: Twenty-six lectures are normally delivered as one double lecture per week; each of the two projects is expected to require approximately 25 hours; no total weekly workload is stated.

course_information.lecturer: Dr S. Achari; Dr M. R. Dangor
course_information.prescribed_materials: No prescribed textbook stated.
course_information.scope: Macroeconomics including scarcity policy GDP inflation unemployment taxation supply and demand; microeconomics and business planning including marketing costing accounts cash flow ratios budgeting and risk; responsible AI-enabled engineering entrepreneurship.

rules.condition_description: ELEN2020A (Software Development I) and ELEN2016A (Electronics I)
rules.plain_language: Before registering for this module, you must have completed ELEN2020A (Software Development I) and ELEN2016A (Electronics I).
